paras: Google Quantum AI published new results in <g>Science</g> this week, run on its Willow chip.
A method called "magic state cultivation" made a key ingredient for big quantum calculations <g>about 40x less error-prone</g>.
<u>Making these "magic states" can eat up to 95% of a quantum computer's capacity, so this is a real bottleneck.</u>

items.l: fidelity of the states that passed

slides.source: Google Quantum AI via CoinDesk, Decrypt

paras: Bitcoin wallets are locked with elliptic-curve cryptography. A big enough quantum computer could work out a <r>private key from a public key</r>.
Google estimated in March that this would take <g>fewer than 500,000 physical qubits</g>.
<u>The oldest coins, from Satoshi's era, have had their public keys exposed since they were mined.</u>

items.l: qubits to break BTC keys (Google est.)

paras: Only about <r>8 in 100</r> attempts pass Google's checks. The rest get thrown away.
<u>This does not make an attack on Bitcoin 40x cheaper.</u>
Cracking RSA-2048 would need magic states about <g>a million times cleaner</g> than today's. Nobody has run Shor's algorithm against Bitcoin.

items.l: Bitcoin keys broken by quantum so far
